question: Should OpenClaw core add native cross-gateway session messaging for `sessions_send`/`sessions_spawn`, or keep gateway-local semantics and expose only plugin/MCP bridge seams for this use case?
rationale: The requested behavior is real and source-reproducible, but it changes gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, message delivery, and config/security surfaces that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design Core Contract First
options.body: Define peer identity, authorization scopes, replay/idempotency, URL policy, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing core cross-gateway messaging.

options.title: Bridge Through Plugins Or MCP
options.body: Keep core session tools gateway-local and add only the missing extension seams needed for an external bridge or MCP integration to implement routing safely.

options.title: Fold Into Broad Federation FRD
options.body: Pause the concrete session-tool implementation until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 resolves the broader bridge protocol and identity model.

recommendation.title: Design Core Contract First
recommendation.body: Define peer identity, authorization scopes, replay/idempotency, URL policy, session visibility, and upgrade behavior before landing core cross-gateway messaging.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses current session-tool, gateway config, and security-boundary code paths where this owner candidate has the strongest available current-main history signal.
